Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/codepilot-appimage.git...

Analyzing codepilot-appimage AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is safe for the narrow gate of `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

The top-level scope contains only standard variable assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `depends`, etc.) with no command substitution, eval, or any executable code. There is no `pkgver()` function, so no version-update logic runs at source-evaluation time.

The source arrays download from expected locations: the project's own GitHub releases (`github.com/op7418/CodePilot`), its own main branch for the icon, and the maintainer's own missing-aur repo for the desktop file. SHA256 checksums are provided and not skipped. The `prepare()` and `package()` functions (which chmod the AppImage and install files) are out of scope for this gate since `--nobuild --noprepare` prevents their execution. Downloading the AppImage binary writes a file to disk but does not execute it.

No malicious patterns detected: no obfuscated code, no exfiltration, no curl|bash patterns, no unexpected remote hosts.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard AppImage PKGBUILD with safe sources and no risky top-level code.</summary>
</security_assessment>
